currentContext.business: Greenply manufactures and markets interior decor and interior infrastructure products - plywood and blockboard, MDF, decorative veneers, flush doors, speciality plywood and PVC products - and also supplies furniture hardware and fittings through a global partnership. It sells to residential, commercial and industrial end-users through a pan-India distribution network of distributors, dealers and retailers, and makes speciality plywood for railways, automobiles and construction-specific architectural structures. The Company operates plywood and allied units at four locations, an MDF plant run through a wholly owned subsidiary, and a joint-venture furniture hardware and fittings unit.

currentContext.expansion: Greenply currently operates five manufacturing facilities across West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Nagaland and Gujarat, with a sixth plywood site in Odisha at work-in-progress stage. Plywood and allied manufacturing runs from Tizit (Nagaland), Kriparampur (West Bengal), Sandila (Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh) and Bamanbore (Gujarat), with total plywood and allied capacity of 52.80 Mn SqM pa; the Company states that with the new capacity operational this will rise to 66.3 Mn SqM pa. MDF is manufactured at Vadodara, Gujarat, through a wholly owned subsidiary, with capacity of 3,00,000 CBM pa and a further new capacity of 2,10,000 CBM pa announced. Management states that, in alignment with its growth agenda and to address rising MDF demand, the Company is preparing to expand its MDF production capacity. The Board approved a new MDF production line at the Vadodara facility entailing a capital investment of ₹425 Crores to add 700 CBM of daily capacity; once commissioned in Q2 FY 2027-28 the facility's capacity rises from 1,000 CBM per day to 1,700 CBM per day, which management describes as making it one of India's largest MDF manufacturing complexes. Management frames the investment as reflecting conviction that MDF will remain a growth engine, supported by growing demand from the furniture, interiors and construction sectors, and notes that MDF today contributes nearly one-fourth of revenues. Fourth-quarter FY 2025-26 was the first fully operational quarter following completion of the earlier MDF capacity expansion. Alongside physical capacity, the Directors' Report states that the Company has prioritised expanding production capacities across its product segments while integrating cutting-edge technologies into manufacturing, aimed at improving operational efficiency, product quality and competitive position.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and price volatility
risks.note: Volatility in the supply or cost of raw materials can impact profitability and disrupt operations, threatening production consistency and complicating cost management; dependence on a steady timber supply exposes the Company to shortages that could affect production continuity. Mitigation is to situate manufacturing facilities close to major raw material sources and plantation zones and to use strategic sourcing and long-term sustainability initiatives.

Shifts in government policies or regulations - particularly those impacting raw material sourcing - can reshape the industry landscape, disrupt manufacturing operations, reduce efficiency and influence the Company's long-term strategic direction. Mitigation is responsible sourcing practices and plants located near compliant plantation zones.

The entry of new players, rising imports and rival innovations can intensify competition and put pressure on pricing and margins; the Company relies on a diverse product portfolio across plywood and allied categories to differentiate and respond to shifting trends.

risks.risk: Demand cyclicality tied to the economy and real estate
risks.note: A weak or slowing economy can dampen consumer confidence, reduce disposable income and negatively affect spending in real estate, home furnishings and decor categories - the Company's core demand pools.
Advances in manufacturing technologies could render existing processes less effective, requiring continuous adaptation and investment in modernisation to remain competitive.

risks.risk: Changing consumer preferences and material substitution
risks.note: A move toward alternative materials or new construction methods could reduce demand for traditional plywood, requiring continued innovation and adjustment of the product offering.

Geopolitical tensions or rising fuel costs can drive up logistics expenses and disrupt supply chain functioning; the Company relies on a structured logistics framework and advanced material tracking systems for visibility and resilience.

A shortage of skilled professionals or challenges in retaining talent can hinder productivity and slow organisational growth; addressed through competitive compensation, regular training, upskilling and development programmes.
Negative publicity or reputational setbacks can erode consumer trust and directly affect revenue streams, requiring continuous monitoring for reputational risks and proactive brand protection.

risks.risk: Climate change and physical weather exposure
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as a material risk and opportunity: extreme weather events such as cyclones, floods and wildfires can disrupt operations and global supply chains, introduce volatility in seasonal cash flows, and raise insurance premiums or reduce insurance availability for assets in high-risk areas.

one-line thesis: Broad-based double-digit volume growth resumed in both plywood (+13.8% YoY) and MDF (+24.7% YoY), with consolidated revenue INR724.9 cr (+20.7% YoY) and core EBITDA margin 10.8% (+50bps). Q1 was seasonally/election-disrupted (utilisation dipped to 92-93% in ply vs 98-99% in Q4), and imported-chemical cost spikes from the Middle-East conflict forced 3-5% ply / 7-9% MDF price hikes. New MDF HDF-flooring line commenced 20-Jul-2026; ~INR500 cr FY27 capex funds Vadodara MDF + Odisha greenfield plywood.

- **New MDF HDF-flooring line:** commercial production commenced 20-Jul-2026; in market from end-Jul; potential peak revenue INR75-80 cr (converts ~INR24-25k/CBM plain board → ~INR60-70k/CBM flooring).
- **SAMET furniture JV:** revenue target INR120-150 cr (FY27/FY28); losses to zero by ~mid-FY28 as imports substituted by domestic manufacturing (capex end-FY27/early-FY28).
- **ContiRoll plywood tech:** 2 of 4 factories implemented, 2 more in H1 FY27; P&L gains from Q4 FY27 onwards.
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business (branded building-materials, dealer/distribution driven). Demand momentum described as "encouraging" across both segments; Q1 demand partly missed on capacity/labour constraints and expected to be recouped as utilisation normalises (ply target near 100%, MDF ~80-82% practical ceiling).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Plywood:** revenue INR526.6 cr, vol +13.8% YoY, realization INR265/sqm; utilisation 92-93% (vs 98-99% Q4); ContiRoll higher-moisture pressing tech (better finish + material/labour savings) rolling out.
- **MDF:** revenue INR195.7 cr, ~57,805 CBM (+24.7% YoY), margin 17.3%; new HDF-flooring line live 20-Jul; second MDF line (Vadodara) with ~70% extra capacity at lower capex/CBM than line-1.
- **Furniture & Fittings JV (SAMET):** sale INR13.61 cr, JV PAT loss INR11.48 cr (Greenply share -INR5.74 cr); ~60% of turnover is traded (imported) goods carrying zero/negative gross margin due to EUR/USD; only 2 products (incl. hinges) made in India today; full local manufacturing end-FY27/early-FY28.
- **Entities/capex split:** GIL (parent), GSPL, GSPPL.
growth verticals / optionality:
- MDF flooring (HDF) — new value-added category, peak potential INR75-80 cr, higher realization.
- Odisha greenfield plywood (near Vizag — future South-India timber catchment access); management flagged intent to build yet another plywood facility after Odisha.
- SAMET export optionality: JV partner motivated to source finished goods from India back to their home market on cost advantage.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Imported chemical (adhesive/resin) prices elevated by Middle-East conflict + rising crude; moderated in 2H of Q1 then "going crazy" again in July. Availability no longer a fear (unlike war onset), but prices at new highs.
- Price hikes: MDF effective 7-9% realised (industry took ~15%; balance passed as schemes); plywood 3-5%. Possible further hikes if chemical inflation persists (or pull back MDF discount schemes).
- Timber: seasonal monsoon rise (moisture + harder cutting) — assumed stable going forward; any fall = windfall.
- Interest cost: term loan 7-7.25%, working capital ~7%.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- FY27 capex ~INR500 cr (GIL 47 / GSPL 100 / GSPPL 300).
- MDF flooring line: commissioned 20-Jul-2026 (on time).
- Vadodara MDF line-2 (~70% extra capacity, lower capex/CBM) + Odisha greenfield plywood — "on track within committed timelines" (verify next Q).
- SAMET domestic-manufacturing capex: end-FY27/early-FY28.
capital allocation: - Net debt INR533 cr, D/E 0.57x now; disciplined vs 0.7-0.75 internal ceiling. Peak debt guided ~INR710-730 cr at FY27-end then deleveraging. Capex self-funded through the cycle; cautious lower-capex-per-CBM approach on MDF line-2 to protect ROCE.
risks & watch-items:
- Chemical/crude cost re-acceleration in July → margin & pricing risk.
- Ply utilisation recovery dependent on labour availability normalising post-election disruption.
- SAMET furniture JV: sustained losses, FX-exposed traded-goods model (~60% turnover), flat revenue 3 quarters; breakeven repeatedly pushed (now ~mid-FY28).
- Execution/slippage risk on Vadodara + Odisha commissioning.
- MDF industry oversupply cyclicality (mgmt explicitly acknowledged capacity-glut boom/bust cycles).
management quality / tone: Candid — openly admitted "we lost sales in Q1", conceded 2-year lag vs Century in planning ply hyper-growth ("we paid that price in the last three years"), and honest on SAMET FX pain. Confident but grounded on margin/ROCE math (13-15% ply margins only at ~INR800 cr/qtr scale). Guidance specific and quantified.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Plywood margin is scale-gated, not structural: 10%+ at ~INR600 cr/qtr, 13-15% only at ~INR800 cr/qtr; also cost-apportionment drag on ply eases as MDF/new categories scale (post-demerger the whole cost base loads onto ply on turnover).
- Line-2 switched press from German → Chinese (kept European fibre "heart") — cost/asset-turn optimisation and a reversal of the earlier all-European stance.
- Flooring cannibalises plain-board CBM but is strongly value-accretive (INR24-25k → INR60-70k/CBM).
- Poor BIS enforcement in furniture-fittings (vs strong BIS control in ply/MDF) is the structural headwind letting Chinese hinge imports persist.

hero.oneLiner: Greenply Industries is a four-decade-old, Kolkata-headquartered pan-India interior infrastructure company and one of India's largest branded plywood and MDF manufacturers, positioned to gain from the wood panel industry's shift toward organised, BIS-compliant players.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Greenply Industries is a four-decade-old, Kolkata-headquartered pan-India interior infrastructure company and one of India's largest branded plywood and MDF manufacturers, positioned to gain from the wood panel industry's shift toward organised, BIS-compliant players.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Greenply manufactures and markets interior decor and interior infrastructure products - plywood and blockboard, MDF, decorative veneers, flush doors, speciality plywood and PVC products - and also supplies furniture hardware and fittings through a global partnership. It sells to residential, commercial and industrial end-users through a pan-India distribution network of distributors, dealers and retailers, and makes speciality plywood for railways, automobiles and construction-specific architectural structures. The Company operates plywood and allied units at four locations, an MDF plant run through a wholly owned subsidiary, and a joint-venture furniture hardware and fittings unit.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Volume growth FY27:** Plywood 10%; MDF 25-30%.
- **Margin:** Plywood EBITDA 10%+ (double-digit) for FY27, reaching 13-15% at ~INR800 cr/qtr run-rate; MDF EBITDA 16-17% sustainable at current capacity, +~1% once line-2 operating leverage kicks in (up to ~18%). MDF ROCE target 17-18% medium/long term (vs ~8% FY26).
- **Net debt:** Peak absolute debt ~INR710-730 cr at 31-Mar-2027, D/E 0.75x at peak; below 0.7 within ~6 months; FY28-end ~0.65-0.7.
- **Capex FY27:** ~INR500 cr total — GIL standalone ~INR47 cr (incl. SAMET loss-funding), GSPL ~INR100 cr, GSPPL ~INR300 cr. Vadodara MDF + Odisha greenfield plywood on track within committed timelines.
- **New MDF HDF-flooring line:** commercial production commenced 20-Jul-2026; in market from end-Jul; potential peak revenue INR75-80 cr (converts ~INR24-25k/CBM plain board → ~INR60-70k/CBM flooring).
- **SAMET furniture JV:** revenue target INR120-150 cr (FY27/FY28); losses to zero by ~mid-FY28 as imports substituted by domestic manufacturing (capex end-FY27/early-FY28).
- **ContiRoll plywood tech:** 2 of 4 factories implemented, 2 more in H1 FY27; P&L gains from Q4 FY27 onwards.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects MDF to remain a growth engine, supported by growing demand from the furniture, interiors and construction sectors, with the segment assuming an increasingly larger role as expanded capacity comes on stream
- Operating leverage in MDF as expanded capacity moves to full utilisation was demonstrated by the Q4 margin step-up, which management cites as validation of the investment
- Plywood margins trended higher through the year, reaffirming management's guidance of double-digit margins as the new benchmark for the segment
- Mandatory BIS certification across plywood, MDF and furniture fittings compressed the cost and quality advantages of unorganised and import-reliant players, tilting the competitive landscape toward organised, quality-certified manufacturers
- Enforcement of the Furniture Quality Control Order from February 2026 reshapes compliance, warranty and after-sales standards, improving access to government and institutional demand
- Real estate upcycle with an aspirational shift toward premium housing - residential apartment sales above ₹1 Crore accounted for over 50% of the market in 2024 and luxury homes above ₹5 Crore grew 80% year-on-year
- Government focus on affordable housing and urban infrastructure, expansion of home financing and fiscal incentives for home ownership continue to catalyse demand
- MDF share of the Indian wood panels market rising from 20% in FY 2019-20 to 30% in FY 2024-25 and expected to approach 45% by FY 2029-30, driven by modular furniture adoption, evolving design preferences and faster replacement cycles
- Indian wood panels market valued at approximately ₹550 billion in FY 2023-24 and projected to expand to nearly ₹885 billion by FY 2029-30
- Indian MDF industry capacity utilisation expected to improve from 51% in FY 2023-24 to 72% in FY 2025-26 as demand catches up with fresh capacity additions, indicating a healthier demand-supply balance
- MDF industry remains relatively consolidated with the top four players accounting for nearly 70% of installed capacity, reinforcing a focus on quality, scale and operational efficiency
- India's furniture market expanding from USD 29.27 billion in 2025 to USD 31.51 billion in 2026 and expected to reach USD 45.52 billion by 2031 at a 7.63% CAGR
- Indian plywood market generated USD 7 billion revenue in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 10 billion by 2033, with a clear shift from unorganised to organised players as consumers prioritise quality assurance, brand reliability and warranty-backed products
- Urbanisation, rising disposable income, growing housing demand, product premiumisation and preference for branded products are the stated demand drivers for wood panels
- Management expects leverage to moderate as new capacities generate superior returns, even though debt may increase temporarily during the ongoing capex cycle
- The Ecotec expansion and marketing investments of FY 2025-26 yielded measurable volume traction in the mid-value segment
- New product vectors - water-repellent plywood, HDF flooring and PVC/WPC - are positioned to leverage existing brand equity and distribution to address fast-growing adjacent categories

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Greenply currently operates five manufacturing facilities across West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Nagaland and Gujarat, with a sixth plywood site in Odisha at work-in-progress stage. Plywood and allied manufacturing runs from Tizit (Nagaland), Kriparampur (West Bengal), Sandila (Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh) and Bamanbore (Gujarat), with total plywood and allied capacity of 52.80 Mn SqM pa; the Company states that with the new capacity operational this will rise to 66.3 Mn SqM pa. MDF is manufactured at Vadodara, Gujarat, through a wholly owned subsidiary, with capacity of 3,00,000 CBM pa and a further new capacity of 2,10,000 CBM pa announced. Management states that, in alignment with its growth agenda and to address rising MDF demand, the Company is preparing to expand its MDF production capacity. The Board approved a new MDF production line at the Vadodara facility entailing a capital investment of ₹425 Crores to add 700 CBM of daily capacity; once commissioned in Q2 FY 2027-28 the facility's capacity rises from 1,000 CBM per day to 1,700 CBM per day, which management describes as making it one of India's largest MDF manufacturing complexes. Management frames the investment as reflecting conviction that MDF will remain a growth engine, supported by growing demand from the furniture, interiors and construction sectors, and notes that MDF today contributes nearly one-fourth of revenues. Fourth-quarter FY 2025-26 was the first fully operational quarter following completion of the earlier MDF capacity expansion. Alongside physical capacity, the Directors' Report states that the Company has prioritised expanding production capacities across its product segments while integrating cutting-edge technologies into manufacturing, aimed at improving operational efficiency, product quality and competitive position.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong brand recognition built over four decades, with the Company described as one of the largest interior infrastructure brands in India
- Strategically positioned, multi-location manufacturing network across Nagaland, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat that supports an efficient supply chain and pan-India availability
- Robust pan-India distribution network of distributors, dealers and retailers servicing 1,100+ cities, towns and villages
- Diversified product portfolio spanning premium to mass-market price points, covering plywood, blockboard, MDF, veneers, doors and PVC products
- Track record of industry-first innovations including zero-emission (E-0) plywood - described as India's first zero-emission plywood - and fire-retardant plywood
- Compliance credibility under the mandatory BIS/QCO regime, which widens the gap versus unorganised players and low-quality imports
- Deep industry expertise in a workforce of more than 5,500 employees and workers as of March 31, 2026, and sustained R&D investment
- Credit rating of AA- (Banking Facilities - Long term) from India Ratings & Research underpinning a dependable credit profile
- Vertical presence in a timber-linked supply chain with FSC Forest Management and Chain of Custody certification

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Overseas write-down] Q4 FY26 PAT was hit by exceptional items of Rs 15.2 crs relating to the Dubai entity GMEL — Rs 9.48 crs provision for financial liability in GMEL, Rs 2.70 crs provision for diminution in value of the investment against a 19% stake in GMEL, and Rs 2.98 crs loss allowance against advance paid.

- [FX exposure] MDF-business borrowings carry a forex exposure disclosed separately as "Forex (Gain)/Loss on borrowings" and treated as an adjustment to finance cost, which swings reported MDF PAT materially between quarters.
- [Institutional register] Largest disclosed institutional holders at 30 June 2026 are Mirae Mutual Fund 12.75% (domestic ELSS plus two foreign Mirae vehicles), HDFC MF 7.17%, Tata MF 5.77%, Canara Robeco 2.62%, Bandhan 2.11%, Aditya Birla 1.12% and SBI Contra Fund 1.08%.
